known.title: bunfig.toml sets minimumReleaseAge to 4320, which Bun reads in seconds, so the three-day quarantine becomes 72 minutes.
known.summary: bunfig.toml:6 sets `minimumReleaseAge = 4320`. The comment at bunfig.toml:4-5 and the text at .github/AGENTS.md:108 say that this value keeps the three-day quarantine of pnpm-workspace.yaml. The deleted pnpm-workspace.yaml:2 gave the same number in minutes: `minimumReleaseAge: 4320 # minutes = 3 days`. Bun reads the number in seconds. The Bun install page says: 'Bun filters out package versions published more recently than the specified threshold (in seconds) during installation.' and 'A number is in seconds.' Its bunfig example for three days is `minimumReleaseAge = 259200 # seconds` (https://bun.sh/docs/pm/cli/install, section Minimum release age). Checked locally: `bun install --help` of Bun 1.4.4 prints '--minimum-release-age=<val> Only install packages published at least N seconds ago'. Thus the gate is 4320 seconds, that is 72 minutes, not three days. The plan keeps the three-day quarantine (Research, Supply-chain policy; step:manifest_and_lockfile; A8), and .github/AGENTS.md:102 says that each supply-chain mitigation is load-bearing. Scenario: a malicious version is published two hours before `bun add` or `bun update` resolves it. The pnpm gate refused this version. Bun now installs it.

known.title: package.json leaves out trustedDependencies, so Bun's built-in trust list runs the claude-code postinstall on every install.
known.summary: The PR deletes pnpm-workspace.yaml and with it `allowBuilds: {'@anthropic-ai/claude-code': false}`. package.json has no `trustedDependencies` field (package.json:17-18). bunfig.toml:14-16 and .github/AGENTS.md:109 say that Bun runs the lifecycle scripts of a dependency only when package.json lists it, so a missing field denies every script. This reading is wrong. The Bun lifecycle page says: 'A curated list of popular npm packages with lifecycle scripts is allowed by default.' Its table says that with 'trustedDependencies omitted' the allowed packages are 'The packages in Bun's built-in list (npm sources only).', and that only `trustedDependencies: []` allows 'No packages, including none from the default list.' (https://bun.sh/docs/pm/lifecycle, section Behavior of the trustedDependencies field). The built-in list contains `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/install/default-trusted-dependencies.txt, line 2; `bun pm default-trusted` of Bun 1.4.4 also lists it). Checked locally with this package.json, bun.lock, and bunfig.toml: after `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, `bun pm untrusted` reports 'Found 0 untrusted dependencies with scripts.'. With `"trustedDependencies": []` it lists the claude-code `[postinstall]: node install.cjs` as blocked. Thus every `bun install`, local or in a CI job, runs the claude-code postinstall and puts the binary of approximately 230 MB in place. This breaks the plan (Research, Supply-chain policy: keep every lifecycle script of a dependency denied; A12 expects a placeholder under 1000 bytes) and the load-bearing mitigation list of .github/AGENTS.md:102-111.

known.title: bunfig.toml leaves out linker = "isolated" because it expects Bun 1.4 to default to it, but this single-package project gets the hoisted linker.
known.summary: bunfig.toml:8-12 sets only `hoist = false`. Its comment says that Bun 1.4 installs with the isolated linker by default. The Bun docs give another default for this project. The install page says: 'New single-package projects: `hoisted` (traditional npm behavior)' (https://bun.sh/docs/pm/cli/install, section Default strategy). The isolated-installs page gives `configVersion` 1 without workspaces the default linker `hoisted`, and says: 'In workspaces, v1 uses the isolated linker by default; otherwise it uses hoisted linking.' (https://bun.sh/docs/pm/isolated-installs, section Default behavior). bun.lock:3 has `"configVersion": 1`, and package.json has no `workspaces` field. Checked locally with Bun 1.4.4: `bun install --frozen-lockfile --offline` with this bunfig.toml makes no `node_modules/.bun`. With `linker = "isolated"` it makes the store. Effect 1: the hoisted layout (https://bun.sh/docs/pm/isolated-installs, Comparison with hoisted installs: 'Packages can access any hoisted dependency') lets a package import a dependency that it never declared. The plan keeps the isolated layout (Research, Install layout; step:manifest_and_lockfile; A13 `ls -d node_modules/.bun`). Effect 2: installFingerprint reads `node_modules/.bun` (scripts/lib/gate-memo.mjs:115-118). The ENOENT comes after the root read, so it throws 'cannot digest node_modules' (gate-memo.mjs:135-137). computeGateKey then returns a null key (gate-memo.mjs:147-151), and the gate memo never hits. Checked: computeGateKey on the hoisted install returned `key: null` with that reason.
